solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird pocketing cut for crate

indicators.note: a bird pocketing something holds it inside, so the bird's letters go around the cut

parts.note: a jay is a crow-family bird
to lop is to cut off branches

explanation.surface: A bird swallows something cut, apparently for a packing crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for a battered old car, as is the word for a rattletrap motor.

clue.text: A flying elephant?

parts.note: a large passenger aircraft is a big beast in the air; elephants are traditionally nicknamed this way too

explanation.surface: A question about an elephant that flies, like the Disney cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boeing 747 is a jumbo jet, and the word is also a classic name for an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-bodied airliner is an elephant-sized craft in the sky; an elephant is commonly called this.

clue.text: Traditions lie in tatters for legendary singer

parts.note: lore is a body of traditions and folk knowledge

indicators.note: torn to pieces, so the letters of the little word are scattered

explanation.surface: Traditions lie in ruins, the legend of a singer debunked.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine siren of German legend whose song lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Shooting game, agony unlikely without bullets, for a start

parts.note: pain is agony

indicators.note: without means outside, so the unlikely word goes around the start of the bullets

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one

indicators.note: for a start means just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A shooting game would be agony if, improbably, nobody had bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat game where players fire dye-filled pellets at each other.

clue.text: Bones more rigid, did you say?

indicators.note: the question asks whether we heard it, so the sound of a word is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: sterner means stricter, more rigid

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether they heard 'bones more rigid' correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent STERNER and STERNA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of sternum, the breastbone, so these are anatomical bones of the chest.

clue.text: Path that's right in the end

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the end word

parts.note: the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A path that turns out right in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A track or footpath through countryside.

clue.text: Warning raised by the Turks?

definitions.meaning: a signal of danger, as on a beach or race track
the Turkish national flag is red with a white crescent and star

explanation.surface: A warning hoisted by Turkish forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger signal is literally a crimson banner, and Turkey's flag is crimson.

clue.text: Deviation in nearby car after swerving

indicators.note: a swerving car veers about, so the phrase's letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A deviation shown by a car nearby that has swerved.
explanation.definitionFit: A departure from the normal course, a straying from what is expected.

clue.text: Clever clogs producing sculpture of Artemis

indicators.note: a sculpture shapes material into a new form, so the name's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A know-all turns out a statue of the Greek goddess Artemis.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever clogs is British slang for a know-it-all, a smart alec type of person.

clue.text: Sardine at sea — more covered on the beach?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the fish's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sardine swimming offshore, compared with one lying on the beach coated in grit.
explanation.definitionFit: On a beach one gets coated in grains, so something with more grains clinging to it is grittier, the comparative adjective.

clue.text: Blooming thing put on tip, bilge

indicators.note: in a down clue being put on means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: a poppy is a flower, something that blooms
to cock is to tilt or tip, as in cocking a hat

explanation.surface: A flower is placed on a tip, rubbish in the bilge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for nonsense, as is this word for drivel.

clue.text: Author's written about giant cylindrical object

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the author's name is set down backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot or George Eliot, the author, with 's as a link
a troll is a giant of Scandinavian folklore

explanation.surface: A writer has produced a book about a giant, perhaps a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A loo roll is a tube of paper wound on a cardboard core, a cylinder described deadpan.

clue.text: Supposed drunkard, not entirely witty, knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over lies the other way round, so the letters run backwards
not entirely means a final letter is lost from the word

parts.note: droll means amusing, witty

explanation.surface: A man thought to be a drinker, not very funny, falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims DROLL to DROL; 'knocked over' reverses it. The definition alludes to the idiom 'drunk as a lord'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'drunk as a lord' makes a peer the proverbial heavy drinker, hence 'supposed'.

clue.text: Islamic denomination claims victory for Hindu god

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Shia is one of the two main branches of Islam

explanation.surface: A branch of Islam claims a triumph over a deity of another religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The destroyer deity of the Hindu trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu.

clue.text: Shoot round shopping complex, nothing much to say

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shoot goes around the complex

parts.note: a stalk is a plant's shoot or stem
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A film shoot around a shopping mall, with little dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite chit-chat about trivial things, conversation with no substance.

clue.text: Shut up about grey novel that was written by Ibsen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shut-up word goes around the rest

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut up or confined

indicators.note: novel means new, so the colour's letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A book with a grey cover is locked away, as if a lost Ibsen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' signals the anagram; Ibsen wrote plays, not novels, so the surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist's verse play of 1867, famous with Grieg's incidental music.

clue.text: Delight outlining centre of clever technical drawing

indicators.note: outlining means surrounding, so the delight word goes round the centre

parts.note: elation is great delight

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Delight at a clever technical drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' clever gives EV, the two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect's drawing of one face of a building seen straight on.

clue.text: General, a believer

definitions.meaning: ... in its old sense means universal or wide-ranging, as in ... tastes
a member of the Roman ... church, a person of faith

explanation.surface: A general turns out to be a person of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-ranging tastes are called catholic, and a Roman church member is one too.

clue.text: Save the worst half, supposedly?

definitions.meaning: to ... resources is to use them sparingly
a joke on 'better half', a wife; her partner is presumably the worse one

explanation.surface: An instruction to rescue the worse half of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to husband, and a married man is jokingly his wife's worse half.

clue.text: Try the shell of eggs, perhaps?

indicators.note: a shell is the outside of something, so only the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: say means for example, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone suggests trying an eggshell, perhaps as a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an essay, as in a first essay at something.

clue.text: Month carrying council leader on the staff

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the month goes around the leader

parts.note: Sept is short for September

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: re means on or about

explanation.surface: A month in which the council leader is on the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod carried by a monarch, a kind of staff of office.

clue.text: Pro patria, legion under surveillance on every front

indicators.note: each word's front is its first letter, taken from every word in turn

explanation.surface: A patriotic legion is watched on all fronts, like an army in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro is an advantage, as in pros and cons, which is also called a positive point.

clue.text: Stuff in sea not designed for US port

indicators.note: in places the stuffing within the reworked letters
something designed has been arranged, so the letters of the phrase are set out afresh

parts.note: to cram is to stuff full

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack something into a sea that was not meant for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' signals the anagram of the sea phrase, and 'in' places the stuffing word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: California's state capital, a deepwater inland port on the Sacramento River.

clue.text: Save an extra item

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to save them

explanation.surface: Keeping an extra item in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To show mercy is to save, and a reserve tyre or part is an extra.

clue.text: Idea that may be sent up

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means read upwards, and this word reads the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An idea that might be mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief held true, a guiding idea.

clue.text: Curved items round the twist

explanation.surface: Bent objects send someone crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is famously curved, and going this way is slang for going mad.

clue.text: Heavyweight after light starter tucked into great dried meat

indicators.note: the pieces are tucked into the other word, placed inside it

parts.note: big means great

indicators.note: after puts the heavyweight piece behind the starter
a starter is the opening, so just the first letter is used

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer tucks into a great meal after a light first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African snack of cured strips, akin to jerky.

clue.text: Name on papers held by important organ

indicators.note: being held by means sitting inside, so the pieces go within the other word

parts.note: key means crucial, important

indicators.note: in an across clue on means following, so the name comes after the papers

parts.note: ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A name written on documents held by an important body or organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the pair of bean-shaped organs that filter the blood.

clue.text: Throw Austen's letters out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the novelist's letters are mixed up

parts.note: Jane Austen the novelist, the 's being a possessive with no letter

explanation.surface: Someone throws away Jane Austen's correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider is to dislodge them from the saddle.
